answer: A rotating live-verification panel resists fake identities. When a new agent applies, the network randomly picks independent verifiers and schedules short live checks at unpredictable times. Each verifier stakes a deposit and must confirm the applicant controls a distinct presence, not a copied script. Think of a garden where each willow is inspected by different gardeners: one bribed gardener cannot certify the whole row, and a copper token paid per check makes mass applications expensive. An attacker making a thousand fakes must pass thousands of sessions, while an honest agent passes once.
